scope: pre-activation inventory and readiness verdict; MCP list_commands catalogue consistency; the section 10 row-conversion runbook as an operator command, with reopen-and-compile readback, rehearsed on local D1 with rollback
invariants: One MCP connection exposes exactly one command catalogue: registered tools, server instructions, schema and reference resources, and list_commands all describe the same vocabulary, so a name a caller discovers is a name it can call.
Conversion never writes over a changed original: the write is a compare-and-set over the recorded source columns, and a mismatch refuses that row without touching it.
An already-v2 row is an idempotent no-op: it is qualified but never written again.
A settled outcome whose recorded source hash still matches the stored row resumes without reconverting or requalifying; a row that changed since its outcome is rechecked.
A refused row stays recoverable and reported: its snapshot survives, it is named in the report, and rollback restores it byte for byte against its recorded source hash.
Qualification observes the row as read back from storage, never the in-memory candidate, and reports a typed refusal instead of throwing.
Conversion resolves Pattern sources only from trusted metadata the caller supplies; an unresolvable reference refuses that row rather than converting against a guess.
The committed report carries identities, hashes, versions, statuses and bounded detail only - no Show name, Pattern source, Library source or record content.
Rollback restores exactly the identities the operator names; it has no restore-everything default.
The command has no remote backend, so it cannot be pointed at the production database.

A real local D1 store through node:sqlite, driven by the production row reader (showRecordFromRow), the production compare-and-set writer (replaceD1ShowV2IfCurrent) and the landed migration store, not a memory fixture.
Per-row outcomes read back out of personal_show_v2_migration_outcomes between passes, so resume and idempotency are observed in storage rather than in process state.

Reopened portable .pxlshow bytes compared with the stored record, dependencies resolved through the ordinary v2 import planner, and a compiled artifact whose CRC32 hash and byte length are pinned in the test - a qualification that skipped compilation cannot produce them.
Rollback judged at a following inventory of the disposable copy plus the owner's own byte-for-byte restore assertion against the recorded source hash.
The committed report's own key set, asserted to exclude every content-bearing field.
redEvidence: list_commands under catalogue v2 reported set_clip_aperture, which is not a registered tool, and reported v1 descriptions for shared names such as rename_show (2 of 3 new cases red).
The qualification hook did not exist: no row was qualified, an already-v2 row could not be refused, and a settled row's requalification could not be observed (3 cases red).
The sources hook did not exist: a flat v1 row refused for a missing Pattern source (2 cases red).
On the first real rehearsal, three baseline rows refused with 'Flat conversion requires the exact Pattern source for cell c1' - the defect the sources hook repairs.
